transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been having trouble sleeping for about three months now, and it's making me feel exhausted. It started around the time I retired.
Could you tell me how the trouble sleeping is affecting your daily life, if at all, and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?

I'm too tired to get much done on my allotment these days, and I find myself dozing off in the chair in the afternoon. As for allergies, I don't have any that I know of — no bad reactions to medicines.

Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have recently started or changed, including what they’re for and the dose if you know it, and also about any past health problems, operations, or hospital stays you’ve had?

I take losartan 50 mg once a day for my blood pressure, and tamsulosin 400 micrograms at night for an enlarged prostate. I've also been taking some over-the-counter sleeping tablets from the pharmacy, diphenhydramine, most nights for the last three weeks. As for past health problems, it's just the high blood pressure and the prostate trouble — I haven't had any operations or hospital stays.
On a scale from 0 to 10, how bad would you say your trouble sleeping is?
I'd say it's about a 7 out of 10. I'm only getting around four hours of sleep a night and I feel shattered.
Can you tell me in your own words what your trouble sleeping is like for you, including where or when you notice it most and anything that seems to make it better or worse?

I just can't get off to sleep at all at night — that's the main thing. It seems worse after I've had a late evening watching TV, and I do notice it's a bit better on the days I've been out for a long walk.
Other than feeling shattered, is there anything else you’ve noticed along with the trouble sleeping that you’d like to mention?
My mood has been a bit low at times since I retired, though I haven't had any thoughts of harming myself. I don't snore loudly as far as I know, and I've never nodded off while driving.

When you think about the trouble sleeping, where in your night does it mostly sit for you — is it right at the start when you're trying to drop off, is it somewhere in the middle of the night, or toward the early morning, or you're not sure?
Actually, thinking about it more carefully — I do fall asleep fine, usually around 11 pm. The problem is I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning and I just can't get back to sleep after that.
Most nights, is it can't get off to sleep or waking at 3 or 4?
I wake at 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep — that's the real problem. I shouldn't have said I can't get off to sleep; I do fall asleep fine at about 11.

Besides the losartan, tamsulosin, and the over-the-counter sleeping tablets you mentioned, is there anything else you take — any other medicines or tablets, regular or occasional, new or changed recently?
No, that's everything — just those three. Nothing else in the way of medicines or tablets.
What's been worrying you most about this, and what would you really like to get out of today's visit?

Honestly, what worries me most is just feeling so tired all the time and not being able to function properly. What I'd really like is for the doctor to give me some proper sleeping tablets to help me get a full night's sleep.

You've told me about your high blood pressure and enlarged prostate, and that you haven't had any operations or hospital stays. Is there anything else from your past health that you think I should know about?
No, I don't think so — it's just the blood pressure and the prostate, really. Nothing else that comes to mind.
Is there anything else you've noticed or would like to add about your sleep or how you've been feeling?
No, I think that covers it. I just want to get back to sleeping through the night properly.
When sleep is difficult, where do you notice that most — in your head, in your body, or in both, or are you not sure?
I'm not really sure — I'd just say I feel worn out all over, more than anything specific in my head or my body.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
